title: Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO, probes continue
since_label: Fri 6 Nov close, the last price before the weekend reports
status: NBC News reports Nvidia closed down 3.9% on Wed 25 Nov, its second straight daily drop after a 31% jump Monday on Huang's return; Yahoo Finance reports Bernstein, Oppenheimer and StoneX have since upgraded the stock, and the Jerusalem Post, citing the Washington Post, reports Pentagon officials considered using the Defense Production Act to get Huang reinstated. BigGo Finance reports Nvidia's internal investigation is still active, and Politico, cited by Yahoo, reports Huang faces closed-door House interviews on 1 Dec, general counsel Tim Teter on 2 Dec and a public Senate Banking hearing on 3 Dec.
why: Nvidia is the anchor of the AI trade and one of the heaviest weights in the Nasdaq, which alts follow.
next_label: House closed-door interview with Huang, Teter 2 Dec, Senate hearing 3 Dec
sources: Nvidia, NBC News, Yahoo Finance, Washington Post, Jerusalem Post, Politico, BigGo Finance, CNN, SCMP

title: MSCI drops Strategy from its indexes
since_label: Wed 11 Nov close, before MSCI's after-hours announcement
status: FinanceFeeds reports bitcoin was near $60,686 on Thu 26 Nov, up about 6% in 24 hours but down about 22% for November, as spot ETFs log a record $5.39B of monthly outflows; Investing News reports Strategy raised its buyback cap to $4B and holds 851,305 BTC at an average cost of about $75,446. MSCI's deletion takes effect after the 30 Nov close, and it is still open whether other index providers will follow.
why: Strategy is the largest corporate BTC holder, and forced selling of its shares tests the main route equity money takes into bitcoin.
sources: MSCI, Strategy, FinanceFeeds, Investing News, Benzinga, crypto.news, FXStreet

title: US proposes new tariffs on China, EU and 12 others
since_label: Tue 24 Nov 13:00 UTC, before the WSJ tariff report
status: CNBC and Yahoo Finance report that USTR Greer on Wed 25 Nov proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies, including an extra 20% on most Chinese goods on top of existing duties, and Greer told CNBC much of it is already priced in; FinanceFeeds, citing CNBC, reports the Nasdaq Composite recovered from a steep early drop and closed down 0.62%. The proposal goes to public comment and a hearing, and Greer says it likely will not take effect for months, while the AP reports the US-China trade truce expires on 10 Jan 2027.
why: Tariffs on China and the EU hit chip and AI hardware supply chains and feed inflation and Fed hike odds, which weigh on the Nasdaq and crypto together.
next_label: US-China trade truce expires; tariffs await public comment and a hearing
sources: USTR, CNBC, Yahoo Finance, AP, Boston Globe, FinanceFeeds, BBC, The Hill

title: Anthropic IPO, the largest AI listing
since_label: Tue 10 Nov, when the price range was set
status: Yahoo Finance and Investing.com report ANT closed Wed 25 Nov at $82.79, up 1.1%, after an intraday low of $73.85, and 24/7 Wall St reports it briefly traded back above its $83 IPO price; Yahoo Finance shows $84.25 after hours, and US markets are closed Thursday. Yahoo Finance says investors are weighing upcoming lock-up expiries, and the timing of those expiries and of Nasdaq 100 inclusion is still open.
why: A raise this size absorbs cash that would otherwise chase other risk, and its first-day close reprices every AI name.
sources: Yahoo Finance, Investing.com, 24/7 Wall St, StockAnalysis, CNBC, CNN

title: Iran and US trade strikes in the Gulf
since_label: Thu 12 Nov 00:00 UTC, before Iran reported the Sirik strike
status: Reuters, via the Times of Israel, reports Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Thu 26 Nov that two more tankers, one a supertanker carrying over 2 million barrels, hit mines and caught fire north of Oman's Khasab; Arab News reports an earlier Guards claim that an LNG carrier hit a mine Wed evening, which Reuters could not verify. The Jerusalem Post reports Tehran says normal shipping will not resume until the US lifts its naval blockade, and no ceasefire has been announced.
why: CoinDesk cites the Gulf escalation, with the dollar and Fed hike odds, behind the crypto sell-off; oil feeds straight into rate expectations.
sources: Reuters, Times of Israel, Arab News, Jerusalem Post, OilPrice, CNBC, CBS News, CoinDesk
